findings.text: The third requirement is plumbed but inert: the standalone reviewer still cannot see the catalog roster. VERDICT: MUST-FIX. pipeline.py:957 builds existing_names from state.all_names and pipeline.py:1957 places it in the prompt context, replacing the 'not needed for standalone review' empty list. But the two templates _review_single_batch renders (prompt_name is 'sn/review_names' at :1939 or 'sn/review_docs' at :1936) never reference a bare existing_names, nor do the shared partials they include. Jinja resolves an undefined variable to nothing and raises nothing, so the context key is discarded in silence. MEASURED, with a positive control in the same run: rendering sn/review_names with existing_names=['MARKER_CATALOG_ROSTER_ENTRY','photon_radiance_of_hard_xray'] and one nearby_existing_names entry produced 31,851 characters in which MARKER_CATALOG_ROSTER_ENTRY is ABSENT, photon_radiance_of_hard_xray is ABSENT, and MARKER_NEARBY_ENTRY is PRESENT - so the probe demonstrably sees a variable the template does render. Log: /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/runs/review-of-comparators-0955/prompt-render-probe.log, script render_probe.py beside it. The only templates carrying an existing_names block are the compose prompts (generate_name_dd.md:411, generate_name_dd_names.md:200, generate_name_signals.md:38), which is why the spec's premise 'the compose path passes up to 200' was true there and does not transfer here. WOULD THE NODE'S OWN TEST CATCH IT: no, structurally - test_standalone_review_prompt_receives_catalog_names monkeypatches render_prompt to a capture stub and then asserts on the captured context dict, so it verifies the call site it just wrote and never the rendered prompt; it passes unchanged if every review template is deleted. FIX: add a roster block to sn/review_names.md and sn/review_docs.md (the nearby_existing_names block at review_names.md:266 is the shape to copy) and re-point the test at the rendered string, not the context. Prompt templates are outside this node's declared write paths, so this is a coordinator scope decision, not a worker oversight to be blamed - but the node cannot be called landed until it is done.

The unit-anchored channel reproduces, in a new allocator, the per-candidate starvation the node was dispatched to remove from the semantic one. VERDICT: MUST-FIX. enrichment.py:311-341 sets unit_cap = max(k, len(batch_names)) and then loops candidates outside, catalog inside, appending every eligible match and breaking both loops the moment len(unit_anchored) >= unit_cap. There is no per-candidate allowance and no second pass, so allocation is first-come in batch order - exactly what the spec forbade when it said to reuse the share-then-spend shape 'rather than inventing a second one'. The semantic half obeys that instruction; this half does not. MEASURED: three candidates carrying units m, s and eV, against a catalog of 40 accepted cross-base names on m and 3 each on s and eV, k=10 so unit_cap=10. Result: candidate_0 receives all 10 (a_m_00..a_m_09); candidate_1 receives 0 and candidate_2 receives 0, though each has three eligible accepted cross-base comparators present in the catalog. Log: /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/runs/review-of-comparators-0955/unit-comparator-share-probe.log, script unit_share_probe.py beside it. PRODUCTION IMPACT: defaults are neighborhood_k=10 (review/state.py:46) and batch_size=15 (review/state.py:45), so unit_cap is 15 and one candidate on a unit as common as m, s, eV, m^-3 or dimensionless in a 5,130-name catalog can absorb the whole budget, leaving the remaining 14 candidates without the comparator the spec calls 'the only signal that catches a split base'. WOULD THE NODE'S OWN TESTS CATCH IT: no - the unit-anchored test uses a ONE-member batch, where starvation is unrepresentable, and the 25-member test gives every candidate the same unit while passing the batch itself as the catalog, so every candidate is filtered out by batch_ids and the unit channel contributes nothing. FIX: give the unit channel the same share-then-spend pass - collect per-candidate match lists first, grant each max(1, unit_cap // len(batch_names)) in a first pass, then spend the remainder - and add a multi-candidate test whose members carry different units.

k stopped bounding the comparator block and the docstring still calls it a cap. VERDICT: SHOULD-FIX. The dedup loop lost its terminal 'if len(deduped) >= k: break', so the returned neighborhood is now unit_cap + the semantic effective_cap rather than k. At defaults that is up to 15 + 15 = 30 comparator lines where the previous code returned at most 10, and at the shared helper's 60-item hard ceiling (workers.py:1787) up to 120. Every one of them is rendered as a bullet in the 'Nearby Existing Standard Names' block (review_names.md:266-277) of both the system and user prompt paths, so this is a direct, unmeasured token cost on every review batch, and no test pins the returned length. The docstring at :276-278 describes k as 'Base cap for semantic and unit-anchored comparator results', which reads as a bound; it is now a floor for both channels. Either restore an explicit overall cap or state the new bound in the docstring and pin it with a test.

physical_base and comparison_basis are computed and carried to a consumer that discards them. VERDICT: NIT, but it misleads the next reader. The summary dicts now carry physical_base and comparison_basis ('semantic' or 'same_unit_different_physical_base'), and the in-code comment says unit-anchored comparators lead 'so a semantic cap cannot hide the signal'. The rendering loop at review_names.md:272-274 emits only id, description, kind and unit, so the reviewer sees a unit-split comparator as an ordinary nearby name under a heading whose instruction is about duplicate detection. Measured in the same render: both 'comparison_basis' and 'same_unit_different_physical_base' are ABSENT from the 31,851-character prompt. The signal does reach the reviewer as a bullet, so this is not the MUST-FIX above - but labelling it in the template is one line and is what makes the whole second requirement legible.

justifications.durability: The semantic channel is durable - it inherits the shared allocator's per-item first pass, second-pass spend, and the 60-item hard ceiling. The unit-anchored channel is a SECOND allocator, hand-written, first-come, and unfair, which is precisely the shape the spec told the node not to invent. enrichment.py:311-341 iterates candidates in the outer loop and the whole catalog in the inner one, appending every match until len(unit_anchored) >= unit_cap, then breaking BOTH loops (:337-341). There is no per-candidate allowance, so the first candidate carrying a common unit consumes the entire budget. Reproduced (unit-comparator-share-probe.log): three candidates on units m, s and eV against a catalog holding 40 accepted cross-base names on m and 3 each on s and eV; unit_cap = max(k=10, batch=3) = 10; candidate_0 receives 10 comparators and candidate_1 and candidate_2 receive ZERO despite each having three eligible comparators sitting in the catalog. At production defaults (state.py:46 neighborhood_k=10, state.py:45 batch_size=15) unit_cap is 15 and a single candidate on a common unit - m, s, eV, m^-3, dimensionless in a 5,130-name catalog - can take all 15, leaving the other 14 without the signal the spec calls the only one that catches a split base. Second durability cost: the final 'if len(deduped) >= k: break' was removed, so k stopped bounding the return - the neighborhood now grows to unit_cap plus the semantic cap (15+15 at defaults, up to 60+60 at the ceiling) against 10 before, with no test pinning it, while the docstring still calls k a 'Base cap'. Third: physical_base and comparison_basis are attached to every comparator and no template renders either, so a later reader will believe the reviewer can tell a unit-split comparator from a semantic one.
justifications.evidence: The evidence for what was measured is strong and reproducible: a before-state quoted verbatim (one query 'shared cluster description 0 description 1 description 2' for five candidates), a 25-to-25 after count, a real negative control that names its mutation and fails as required, and a baseline/after full-suite pair at d50d42d6 and 0e9218080 whose 23 failure ids are byte-identical, so added failures = 0 is a supported claim and the 7,528-to-7,531 pass delta is exactly the three new tests. The aperture is what fails. The third requirement's test (test_standalone_review_prompt_receives_catalog_names) asserts rendered_contexts[-1]['existing_names'], the CONTEXT DICT it just stubbed render_prompt to capture - it monkeypatches the renderer away and then checks its own input, so it cannot fail on the defect above and would pass identically if every review template were deleted. The assertion that could have failed is on the rendered string. Nothing measures unit-anchored allocation across more than one candidate: test_same_unit_different_base_accepted_name_is_a_comparator uses a ONE-member batch, and test_every_batch_item_contributes_a_vector_query gives all 25 candidates the same unit '1' while its catalog is the batch itself, every member of which is excluded by batch_ids - so the unit channel is inert in that test.
justifications.fit: Idiomatic for this repository. It reaches for the existing proven helper rather than a new one, keeps the summary-only return shape, preserves the batch-member exclusion by padding the search k with len(batch_ids), and guards the empty-batch case up front. Names describe mechanism (unit_anchored, comparison_basis, same_unit_different_physical_base) with no plan or version label anywhere, tests live in tests/standard_names/ under a behaviour-named file, and the gate ran on a SLURM debug partition to a named on-disk log as the repo requires. The docstring is the weak point: it promises k as a cap that is now a floor, and it advertises physical_base and comparison_basis as if they were consumed downstream.
justifications.goal_fidelity: Three requirements were dispatched and one and a half hold. FIRST, the per-item search is exactly right: build_neighborhood_context (enrichment.py:289-310) deletes the cluster-label-plus-first-three-descriptions query and routes every batch member through workers._collect_nearby_name_comparators with per_item_k=k, cap=k, so effective_cap = min(max(cap, len(items)), 60) (workers.py:1826) grows the allowance to the batch size and results_by_item searches every item. The worker's 5-to-1 versus 25-to-25 query counts are the right measurement of that. THIRD, the standalone roster does NOT reach the reviewer. pipeline.py:1957 now sets context['existing_names'], but NO review template reads that variable: grep over imas_codex/llm/prompts/sn/review_names.md, review_docs.md and every shared partial they include (_grammar_reference.md, _exemplars.md, _review_scored_examples.md) returns zero hits for a bare existing_names; the only templates that render it are the COMPOSE prompts (generate_name_dd.md:411, generate_name_dd_names.md:200, generate_name_signals.md:38). Rendered proof with a positive control in the same run: sn/review_names rendered to 31,851 characters with existing_names=['MARKER_CATALOG_ROSTER_ENTRY','photon_radiance_of_hard_xray'] and both are ABSENT, while MARKER_NEARBY_ENTRY from nearby_existing_names in the same context is PRESENT (prompt-render-probe.log). So the node's own headline - the reviewer sees the catalog it is judging against - is not achieved on the roster half; Jinja discards an undefined variable silently, which is why nothing reported it. SECOND, the unit-anchored comparator exists and matches the named live fixture, but its allocation starves the batch - scored under durability.
justifications.scope_discipline: Clean, and deliberately so at the one point where it was tempting. The node reuses _collect_nearby_name_comparators from imas_codex/standard_names/workers.py, which is the exclusive write path of the concurrent node n-the-comparator-share-holds-at-the-production-batch-size; it IMPORTS the helper and edits nothing there, which is the correct move. git show --stat over both commits touches only the five declared paths (enrichment.py, pipeline.py, test_review_catalog_comparators.py, and the two HTML documents). The plan commit is additive only - 81 insertions, 0 deletions - and greps clean for plan-version, plan-modified and plan-status, so the meta lines a worker must not touch were not touched. No terminal status set, no driving followup resolved, nothing pushed or merged, branch left at 1eb1d82ac. Commit subjects are conventional with bodies and carry no plan, sprint or ticket identifier, and no AI attribution. Pre-existing export/error-sibling failures were reported under follow_ons rather than triaged.
